# Continual-ARC demo fixture recovery

Use after a cached program or submitted answer receives an incorrect verdict.

1. Treat rejection as falsification of the complete candidate rule; do not patch colors or coordinates by intuition.
2. Transcribe every available demo as a full grid. Compare dimensions and every cell, recording changed coordinates, values, and unchanged analogues.
3. Keep transcriptions as executable fixtures. Passing the test input, matching selected coordinates, or a plausible geometry does not validate a transform.
4. Form candidate rules that explain every pair, including no-op regions and varying orientations/palettes. Run every fixture after each revision.
5. If candidates remain ambiguous and demos remain, request one that distinguishes them. Do not spend submissions on nearby heuristics after repeated failed rewrites.
6. Submit only output generated by the task program after exact full-grid validation on all demos. Preserve the program after verdict and finish only once the instance is over.

## Pitfalls

- Do not let the newest demo erase earlier counterexamples; all pairs constrain the rule.
